author.note: Date is audit bookkeeping; original authorship date is unknown.

countingMethod: claimsChecked is the conservative count of complete question-answer propositions semantically reviewed, not a count of all factual sentences or exclusively source-verified claims. Corrections count individual logged changes, including qualifications and evidence-gap disclosures.
reviewScope: Full semantic reading of every listed lesson and question field, selected primary-source checks and selected executable examples. Medium confidence; not an exhaustive source/runtime certification.

corrections.reason: Runnable sequence produces one booking row, not two.
corrections.original: On the two-row example, do not expect the index to win.
corrections.correction: On this tiny example, do not expect the index to win.

corrections.reason: retrofit: Insert rule is not built the same way (base 1000, scales by unfrozen fraction, no cap); the bare 'scale factor' linked the ANALYZE 10 % to autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor (0.2).
corrections.original: Separate rules, built the same way, start vacuums after many inserts and start ANALYZE (with a 10 % scale factor, counting inserts too).
corrections.correction: Similar rules start a vacuum after many inserts (autovacuum_vacuum_insert_threshold, 1,000 rows by default, plus 20 % of the table's not-yet-frozen part) and start ANALYZE (50 rows plus 10 % of the table by default, counting inserts, updates and deletes).

corrections.reason: retrofit: Bare 'scale factor' alias removed (cross-subject capture); wording keeps the link precise.
corrections.original: a smaller scale factor of its own
corrections.correction: a smaller vacuum scale factor of its own

corrections.reason: retrofit: Lesson defines MB with 1024 multipliers; 19,200 MB = 18.75 GB.
corrections.correction: about 19,200 MB, nearly 19 GB (18.75 GB counting 1024 MB per GB)

corrections.reason: retrofit: txid_current is in the docs' 'Deprecated Transaction ID' table.
corrections.correction: SELECT pg_current_xact_id(); ... the older txid_current() is deprecated.

corrections.reason: retrofit: AWS: retention period 0–35 days for DB instances; 0 disables automated backups.
corrections.correction: 0 to 35 days; 0 turns automated backups off

corrections.reason: retrofit: Multi-word aliases fall back across subjects and would capture other meanings (persistent data structures, OS thread/semaphore pools, OS buffer cache, DSA hash operations).
corrections.original: aliases 'old versions', 'pool size', 'buffer cache', 'sort operation(s)', 'hash operation(s)', 'scale factor(s)'
corrections.correction: removed; sort-hash-operation now uses 'sort and hash operations', 'sort or hash operation', 'hash-based operations'

corrections.original: connection-limit example: the 101st simultaneous connection attempt is refused
corrections.correction: adds that ordinary roles are refused earlier because superuser_reserved_connections (default 3) reserves slots

corrections.reason: retrofit: Ambiguous wording; max_wal_size can also trigger checkpoints.
corrections.original: checkpoint example: a checkpoint happens at least every 5 minutes
corrections.correction: automatic checkpoints are at most 5 minutes apart, sooner if a lot of WAL is written

corrections.original: flush example: typically a fraction of a millisecond to a few milliseconds
corrections.correction: COMMIT returns only after its WAL has been flushed; with synchronous_commit = off it returns before

corrections.original: streaming-replication example: a few hundred milliseconds behind is typical
corrections.correction: primary_conninfo tells a standby which primary to stream WAL from

corrections.correction: removed; the databases/03 and 04 entries (tuple, seq-scan, explain-postgres, analyze-command, vacuum, autovacuum, pg-class, temp-buffers, megabyte-pg, os-db, pg-stat-statements, orm) link instead

lowConfidence.claim: Exhaustive primary-source support and runtime reproduction of every illustrative example
lowConfidence.reason: Core explanations and all question fields were semantically reviewed, but only selected technical claims were individually source-checked; unexecuted snippets and absent benchmark records are explicitly documented. Version-dependent or performance claims have been qualified.
'Strong lock' is an informal umbrella term, not a PostgreSQL lock mode name; the definition says so and anchors it to ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, which the docs define.

lowConfidence.claim: M_max ≈ w × k × c work_mem estimate
lowConfidence.reason: A rough model labelled as such, not a documented formula; the docs only say total memory can be many times work_mem. Parallel workers, hash_mem_multiplier and per-backend overhead can push real usage above it.

lowConfidence.claim: glossary examples for connection-pool (hundreds of requests a second on 20 connections), os-page-cache (microsecond reads), inclusive-timing (illustrative numbers)
lowConfidence.reason: Illustrative, workload-dependent figures without a primary source.
Sourced to Wikipedia's consistency-model article; the term is standard but has no single primary definition.

gaps: Original benchmark/run records are unavailable; no exact runtime or memory requirement is certified.
Every lesson and question was read semantically. Sources were fetched for selected technical/version-sensitive claims; there is no exhaustive sentence-by-sentence primary-source mapping.
Not every SQL snippet was executed; some are fragments, intentionally erroneous examples or PostgreSQL-specific. Actual execution coverage is recorded in docs/audit-systems.json.

revisions.scope: cross-module and cross-subject glossary leak reconciliation
revisions.notes: Leak reconciliation: removed 7 aliases (cluster-wide, recovery targets, obsolete versions, temporary objects, page ranges, driver parameters, data pages); renamed temporary-object, sequence-object, data-page; connection-limit definition broadened (max_connections default 100 checked against PostgreSQL runtime-config-connection docs); 2 'multiplied by itself' phrases replaced.
